# Acceleration and Sparse Structures

Also called: Sparse Acceleration, Visual Hull Constraints, Hybrid Radiance Caching

## Overview
This family of methods accelerates [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) training and rendering by reducing the computational cost of evaluating the [neural radiance field](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md). It addresses the bottleneck of querying high-dimensional MLPs for every sample point along every ray. Unlike standard uniform or adaptive sampling over the entire scene bounding box, these methods restrict evaluation to [sparse structures](#5-sparse-structures.md) (visual hulls) or use lightweight approximations (caches) to predict radiance, thereby reducing the number of expensive neural network queries [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism across these methods is the reduction of the search space or the replacement of expensive queries with cheaper approximations.

1.  **Spatial Restriction:** Methods like [VaxNeRF](#11379-vaxnerf.md) restrict ray sampling to a sparse subset of the volume, defined by [geometric constraints](#9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md) (e.g., visual hull), eliminating queries in empty space [S1].
2.  **Approximation via Caching:** Methods like Zip-NeRF use hybrid cache systems ([fast cache](#9552-fast-cache-control-variate-radiance-cache.md) + NeRF-cache) to estimate incoming radiance for [importance sampling](#9521-importance-sampling.md), serving as control variates to correct bias while maintaining accuracy with fewer samples [S1].
3.  **Gradient Management:** When using caches as control variates, the "gradient trick" (stop-gradient on the cache estimator) is applied to ensure correct gradient flow to the primary model parameters during joint optimization [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Zip-NeRF Training Procedure](9538-zip-nerf-training-procedure.md)
A two-stage optimization method using a hybrid radiance cache (fast cache + NeRF-cache) to estimate incoming radiance for importance sampling. It sets itself apart by using a fixed small number of samples and direct distance prediction in the fast cache as a control variate, correcting the bias of the NeRF cache.

### [VaxNeRF](11379-vaxnerf.md)
An [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) strategy that restricts ray sampling to the visual hull $V$, defined by the maximum volume compatible with object silhouettes. It sets itself apart by using a single MLP with uniform sampling restricted to voxels inside $V$, eliminating the need for adaptive sampling and reducing the search space.

## Background
The need for acceleration in NeRF arises from the high computational cost of evaluating MLPs for every sample point. [Standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) uses coarse/fine two-stage sampling over the entire bounding box, which is inefficient for large scenes or sparse data. VaxNeRF introduces the visual hull constraint to prune empty space [S1]. Zip-NeRF introduces hybrid caching to handle high-fidelity material models and environment maps efficiently by approximating incoming radiance [S1].
